subject.title: fix(channels): honor configured read target policies

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this host-attested current-conversation authority and fail-closed read-policy contract as the permanent core/plugin boundary?
rationale: The PR changes which runtime facts plugins may trust, when existing reads fail closed, and how bundled versus external plugin provenance is treated; implementation review cannot choose that long-term security and compatibility contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt after reconstruction
options.body: Resolve the current-main conflicts, preserve the reviewed host-owned contract, and require fresh exact-head allowed, denied, upgrade, and provider proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the public surface
options.body: Keep channel-local pre-read authorization but reduce the new public tool-context or bundled-provenance special cases before landing.

options.title: Pause for redesign
options.body: Do not merge this branch until maintainers select a different authorization architecture and migration policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt after reconstruction
recommendation.body: Resolve the current-main conflicts, preserve the reviewed host-owned contract, and require fresh exact-head allowed, denied, upgrade, and provider proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history owns the central plugin-tool and signed Gateway identity surfaces where the permanent contract is enforced.
